slots.hypothesis: The raw minute-return kurtosis mixes two things: trading sparsity (n/k, because Ret has a point mass at 0) and the tail shape c of the minutes that actually traded (kurt+3 = (241/k)*c). The periphery separates the sparsity part out so the GP grows on c alone. It does this three ways: the exact correction mul(add(core,3), sub(1, day_zero_ratio(Ret))); a subtractive version against the Gaussian baseline; and cs_bucket_rank inside deciles of 20-day zero-ratio, longest flat run or price level (tick grid). A cs_winsor step before the EMA stops single-print days from dominating the 20-day average. 12 seeds. Bucket variables with heavy ties (LimitWidth, BoardCode, daily zero-ratio) are left out on purpose to avoid the column-order ramp (pitfall 2).

Intraday price efficiency, meaning serial dependence in 1-minute returns. Seeds use variance ratios std(q-min)/std(1-min) for q=5 and 15, plus a Vwap version; lag-1 and lag-5 autocorrelation on traded minutes only (Vwap is NaN when no trade happens); Boehmer-Kelley style magnitudes |logVR - log sqrt5| and |autocorr|; and path efficiency normalised by sqrt(k) or bucketed within zero-ratio deciles. All are taken as 20-day means, and some are bucketed within price deciles to remove the mechanical tick-grid bounce. The existing head is permutation-invariant, while every seed here depends on the order of the minutes. None of the 5 controls measures intraday serial correlation, and there is no durbin_watson and no convex transform of volatility. 12 seeds.

I've written the round-1 plan for seed 803 and the notebook entry. The admissibility check (scripts/c06_check.py 803 1) prints ADMISSIBLE with exit code 0. Nothing has been evaluated on data yet.

**What I had to work with:** the snapshot has one head, day_kurt(Ret) (score +0.97, direction -1). The locate step returned no ablation, no common-subtree table and no core cards, so that head is the only legal E core this round.

**Slot a (E, core day_kurt(Ret)):** the idea is that the raw kurtosis mostly measures how sparsely a stock trades, not the shape of its returns. Ret is exactly 0 on minutes with no price change, so when only k of 241 minutes move, kurt+3 = (241/k)*c, where c is the tail shape of the minutes that did move. I checked this on random tensors only, not on data: a Gaussian day with 48 active minutes gives kurtosis 10.7, above a fully active t(4) day at 3.1. Multiplying by the active share gives 2.7 and 6.1, so the shape order comes back. The 12 seeds strip out the sparsity part in three ways:
- the exact correction (kurt+3)*(1-zero_ratio);
- a subtractive version against the Gaussian baseline;
- ranking within deciles of 20-day zero-ratio, longest flat run, price level or turnover.

One seed also clips before the 20-day EMA. I did not bucket by LimitWidth, BoardCode or daily zero-ratio: they have so many ties that the buckets would split by column order (pitfall 2).

**Slot b (N, intraday price efficiency):** 12 seeds built on the order of the minutes, which the kurtosis head ignores entirely. They cover variance ratios at 5 and 15 minutes (plus a Vwap version), autocorrelation on traded minutes only, Boehmer-Kelley style |deviation| measures, and path efficiency normalised by sqrt(k). Some are ranked within price or zero-ratio deciles to remove the mechanical bounce from coarse ticks. No durbin_watson, and no convex transforms of volatility.

**R (7 variants of day_kurt(Ret)):** swap the input for Vwap log changes, intraday-rebuilt in_pct(Close,1), or in_madz(Ret,30). Swap the root for day_gini on Ret and on Vwap, or for day_es_ratio_hi / lo.

**Risk to slot a:** if the core itself correlates 0.5 or more with the liquidity control, the slot becomes a plain GP under the rules. I couldn't check this beforehand because the correlation table is computed by the pipeline.

- Slot a: about 45% chance of a head, likely scoring 0.5–0.8 with |rho| to the core of 0.3–0.6.
